testEnvironment:
Test environment: the snapshot is a git repository whose single commit holds
the reviewed tree — its tree hash was compared against the commit under review
when the snapshot was cut. A suite run here collects and runs what a checkout at
that commit does, so a failing or skipped test is a fact about the tree, not
about this copy of it. Its history is that one synthetic commit: 'git log',
'git diff' and every ancestry question answer about the snapshot and never about
the PR.
The Recipe's Test entrypoint and Check step do not run these merge-gating CI steps, and nothing in this review ran them: rebase-check job (pull_request-only branch-currency assertion, not meaningful in a worktree of origin/main); proc-macos job (node --test tests/proc.test.mjs on macOS) (subsumed by the full suite on this macOS host); smoke-omp job (needs pinned omp installed via bun, absent here); install-and-smoke job (needs pinned omp installed via bun and network, absent here).

survived.claim: A dash-led argument placed after a leading `--` but before any path is still dropped silently, with exit 0. This is the same silent-drop class the PR says it closes, and it covers typo'd flags, which the PR text says stay loud.
survived.evidence: In the copy, `./agent-test -- --test-name-pattern=one fx/a.test.mjs` printed `tests 2`, `pass 2` and exited 0. The flag was ignored and a two-test file ran in full. `./agent-test -- --test-name-patern=typo fx/a.test.mjs` and `./agent-test -- --bogus-flag fx/a.test.mjs` also printed `tests 2`, `pass 2` and exited 0. Raw `node --test -- --test-name-patern=typo fx/a.test.mjs` does the same, so node drops everything after `--`. The new guard only fires when $operand is already set. A leading `--` is a flag arm that sets no operand, so the flag after it is waved through. The new test's `-- then flag` row is `t/a.test.mjs -- --flag`, which has a path first, so it does not cover this ordering.
survived.suggested_fix: Track having passed a literal `--`. In the `-*)` arm, once `--` has been seen, refuse any later dash-led argument that is not an existing path. Alternatively refuse a bare `--` outright, since its comment already calls it "no more a path than a flag". Add a test row for `-- --test-name-pattern=one t/a.test.mjs`.

votes.reason: Reproduced in my own copy at the reviewed head (receipt exit 0, kind built). `./agent-test -- --test-name-pattern=one fx/a.test.mjs` printed tests 2 and pass 2 and exited 0, so the flag was dropped. `./agent-test -- --bogus-flag fx/a.test.mjs` did the same. The positive control `./agent-test --test-name-pattern=one fx/a.test.mjs` printed tests 1, so the flag does take effect when it comes before the path. I read the code at agent-test:640-648: the guard fires only when $operand is set, and a leading `--` sets none. I did not run the typo'd `--test-name-patern` variant. The `--bogus-flag` run covers the same case. This is a narrow edge case, but the claim is true of the code as merged. unverified.claim: No logic error found: the refusal fires exactly when a flag-arm argument follows a file, directory or quoted-glob operand. Every behavior the ticket lists as unchanged is unchanged.
unverified.evidence:
In correctness/copy with pt/t/a.test.mjs and pt/d/b.test.mjs (tests one/two), `env -u FORCE_COLOR ./agent-test <args>` gave:
- `pt/t/a.test.mjs --test-name-pattern=one` → exit 1, `agent-test: --test-name-pattern=one comes after a test path…`
- `--test-name-pattern=one pt/t/a.test.mjs` → exit 0, tests 1
- `pt/d --test-only`, `'pt/t/*.test.mjs' --test-only`, `pt/t/nomatch*.mjs --test-only`, `pt/t/a.test.mjs pt/d --test-only`, `pt/t/a.test.mjs --`, `pt/t/a.test.mjs -`, `pt/t/a.test.mjs -x` → each exit 1 with the refusal naming the argument
- `-- pt/t/a.test.mjs` → exit 0, tests 2
- `pt/t/a.test.mjs -dash.test.mjs` (file exists) → reached node: tests 3, pass 2, exit 1, no agent-test: line
- `--test-name-pattern=one` alone → the existing flags-only refusal
- `--import=./pt/setup.mjs --test-name-pattern=one pt/t/a.test.mjs` → exit 0, tests 1
- `-- --test-name-pattern=one pt/t/a.test.mjs` → exit 0, tests 2 (out of scope per the brief)

unverified.claim: The new test passes on the PR tree and kills both directions of the mutation proof the ticket asks for.
unverified.evidence:
Mutants ran in correctness/copy with `node --test tests/agent-test.test.mjs`, FORCE_COLOR and NODE_TEST_CONTEXT unset.
- (a) The refusal block in the flag arm replaced with `:`, run with `--test-name-pattern='flag after a test path'` → exit 1, tests 1, fail 1: '✖ runner: a flag after a test path is refused, not silently dropped by node'.
- (b) `if [ -n "$operand" ]` replaced with `if true`, full file → exit 1, tests 62, fail 4. The failures include '✖ runner: a node --test flag reaches node instead of being read as a path' and the new test.
- Baseline: test-run.log:63 `✔ runner: a flag after a test path is refused…`.

unverified.claim: The loop-head comment says 'each of the nine exits inside this loop is `exit 1`'. The loop now holds 13 such exits: it held 12 before the PR, so the count was already wrong, and the PR adds one more without correcting it.
unverified.evidence: `awk 'NR>=96 && NR<=730 && /exit [0-9]/'` on the snapshot agent-test lists exit-1 calls at lines 253, 344, 382, 390, 398, 406, 428, 534, 539, 603, 608, 649 (new) and 724, which is 13. Line 122 says nine.
unverified.suggested_fix: Drop the number ("each exit inside this loop is `exit 1`") or correct it to 13. Optionally also reword line 107, "the flag arm names nothing and stays silent": the arm still records no operand, but it is no longer silent after one.

unverified.claim: The refusal text says the flag 'comes after a test path' even when the earlier operand is a flag's separate-word value, not a test path. This is the brief's own expected consequence, so only the wording is in question.
unverified.evidence: `./agent-test --import ./pt/setup.mjs --test-name-pattern=one pt/t/a.test.mjs` → exit 1, `agent-test: --test-name-pattern=one comes after a test path, where node does not read it — put node's options before the first test path`. No test path precedes the flag; `./pt/setup.mjs` was counted as the operand. The `--import=./pt/setup.mjs` spelling runs tests 1, exit 0.
unverified.suggested_fix: Optional: say "after an existing path or glob" so a caller using `--import ./x.mjs` can see why it was refused, or name the `--flag=value` spelling in the message.

unverified.claim: No scope creep: the diff changes only the flag arm and its comment in agent-test, plus one new test in the runner's suite. That matches the ticket's Refuse shape and its 'nothing is reordered' constraint.
unverified.evidence: `git apply --stat pr.diff` → `agent-test | 20 +-`, `tests/agent-test.test.mjs | 54 +`, 2 files. The agent-test hunk (pr.diff:5-31) touches only the `-*)` arm at lines 631-651. Grepping plugin/, README.md, AGENTS.md, CONTEXT.md and docs/adr for `test-name-pattern|flags alone|flags-only|#352` found no doc describing the old behavior that would need an update.

unverified.claim: The refusal also fires on legitimate node invocations where an option's value is a separate word naming an existing path. It is loud (exit 1) rather than silent, but it blocks a valid run and its message misdescribes the cause.
unverified.evidence: With `fx/setup.mjs` existing, `./agent-test --import ./fx/setup.mjs --test-name-pattern=one fx/a.test.mjs` exited 1 with `--test-name-pattern=one comes after a test path, where node does not read it`. Node would read that flag, because it comes before the first real file operand. The existing path `./fx/setup.mjs` is the `--import` value, not a test path. The code comment acknowledges the value-as-operand ambiguity but only uses it to justify not reordering.
unverified.suggested_fix: Accept the false refusal as a documented limit, or recognise space-separated value-taking options (`--import`, `--require`, `--test-reporter`, …) so their following word is not recorded as an operand.

unverified.claim: The new test discriminates: disabling, exit-code-flipping, or stream-redirecting the refusal in agent-test each turns it red, and an always-refuse mutant also turns it red via the flag-first control; only unasserted message wording can change while it stays green.
